title: Thoracic aortic aneurysms: dimensions, hemiarch, total arch and elephant trunk techniques
subject: ss-ctvs
refs: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22e Ch 115 (Aortic Aneurysms and Dissection)
2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease
EACTS/STS Guidelines for Diagnosing and Treating Acute and Chronic Syndromes of the Aortic Organ

steps.say: Surgical resection for ascending thoracic aortic aneurysms is governed by strict dimensional criteria. In asymptomatic non-syndromic patients, elective surgery is indicated once maximal external aortic diameter reaches 5.5 centimetres. In patients with bicuspid aortic valves and associated risk factors, the threshold lowers to 5.0 centimetres.
steps.tx: Elective repair of an **ascending aortic aneurysm** is indicated in asymptomatic, non-syndromic patients once the maximum external diameter reaches a **surgical threshold** of 5.5 cm. In individuals with a congenital **bicuspid valve** harboring risk factors such as rapid growth or severe coarctation, the threshold drops to 5.0 cm.

steps.say: Genetic connective tissue disorders require earlier prophylactic surgical intervention. In Marfan syndrome, repair is recommended at 5.0 centimetres, or 4.5 centimetres when family history reveals early dissection or growth exceeds 0.5 centimetres per year. In Loeys-Dietz syndrome, the threshold is 4.5 centimetres due to aggressive vascular fragility.
steps.tx: In hereditary aortopathies such as **Marfan syndrome**, surgery is recommended at an aortic diameter of 5.0 cm, or 4.5 cm with a family history of premature dissection or rapid expansion exceeding 0.5 cm per year. In **Loeys-Dietz syndrome**, high vascular fragility warrants a lower **surgical threshold** of 4.5 cm.

rows: 5.0 cm if undergoing concomitant cardiac surgery
5.0 cm with rapid growth or family history
4.5 cm with family history of dissection or > 0.5 cm/yr growth
4.0 cm with severe TGFBR mutation or tortuosity

steps.say: Ascending aneurysms extending into the proximal transverse arch require hemiarch replacement. Under moderate hypothermic circulatory arrest at 24 to 28 degrees Celsius, the surgeon divides the underside of the arch. Suture the beveled distal Dacron graft along the lesser curvature, sparing the origin of the brachiocephalic vessels.
steps.tx: When aneurysm pathology extends into the proximal arch, an open **hemiarch replacement** is performed under **hypothermic circulatory arrest** at 24 to 28 degrees Celsius. The distal prosthetic graft is beveled and anastomosed along the lesser curvature of the **transverse arch**, leaving the great vessel origins undisturbed.

nodes.label: Cool patient to moderate hypothermia (24 to 28 degrees Celsius)
Arrest systemic circulation and excise distal ascending aorta
Bevel Dacron graft to conform to underside of transverse arch
Complete open distal anastomosis and re-establish systemic perfusion

steps.say: Extensive arch pathology involving the head vessels mandates total arch replacement. The entire transverse arch is resected, and brachiocephalic arteries are reimplanted either as a single island button or using individual branched graft limbs. Branched grafts permit sequential debranching and optimize distal arch hemostasis.
steps.tx: A **total arch replacement** involves resecting the transverse aorta from the innominate origin to the proximal descending aorta. The arch vessels are revascularized using an **island button** patch of native aortic cuff or, more commonly, by individual anastomosis to separate limbs of a dedicated trifurcated **branched graft**.

left.title: Branched Graft Reconstruction
points: Individual prosthetic limbs to each head vessel
Permits sequential reperfusion of cerebral vessels
Eliminates late aneurysm formation in native cuff

right.title: Island Carrel Patch Technique
points: Reimplants all three arch branches in a single cuff
Technically faster with fewer individual anastomoses
Carries risk of late patch aneurysmal redilatation

steps.say: Bilateral antegrade selective cerebral perfusion provides superior brain protection during circulatory arrest. Cannulating the right axillary or innominate artery and the left common carotid artery delivers cold oxygenated blood at 10 to 12 millilitres per kilogram per minute. This technique preserves cerebral metabolic integrity and minimizes stroke risk.
steps.tx: Optimal neurological protection during arch repair utilizes bilateral **antegrade cerebral perfusion** via direct **axillary cannulation** and left carotid catheterization. Infusing cold oxygenated blood at a **perfusion flow rate** of 10 to 12 mL/kg/min maintains cerebral microvascular perfusion and prevents ischemic neurological deficits.

rows: 10 to 15 mL/kg/min; relies on intact circle of Willis
10 to 12 mL/kg/min combined; uniform bi-hemispheric delivery
Cold blood at 300 to 500 mL/min; flushes particulate air/emboli

steps.say: The conventional elephant trunk technique facilitates staged repair of extensive thoracoabdominal aneurysms. The surgeon constructs the distal arch anastomosis and leaves a redundant cylinder of Dacron graft floating free in the proximal descending aorta. In the second stage, this provides a safe landing zone for open or endovascular completion.
steps.tx: The classical **elephant trunk** procedure leaves an unattached, **free-floating Dacron** tube graft suspended within the proximal descending thoracic aorta. This design facilitates subsequent **second-stage completion** via left thoracotomy or endovascular stent deployment, eliminating the need to dissect dense proximal adhesions around the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

nodes.label: Stage 1: Median sternotomy, hypothermic arrest, total arch replacement
Invert Dacron tube into descending aorta as free-floating elephant trunk
Postoperative recovery, interval imaging, and spinal cord assessment
Stage 2: Open thoracotomy or TEVAR completion using elephant trunk landing

steps.say: The modern frozen elephant trunk technique combines open arch surgery with an integrated stented endograft in a single setting. The surgeon deploys the distal stented portion antegradely into the descending aorta under direct vision before completing the arch anastomosis. This achieves immediate descending aortic stabilization and false lumen thrombosis.
steps.tx: The contemporary **frozen elephant trunk** is a **hybrid technique** that unites total arch replacement with an integrated covered stented endograft in a **single-stage operation**. The endograft is deployed antegradely into the proximal descending thoracic aorta under direct vision, inducing immediate false lumen thrombosis and structural stabilization.

left.title: Frozen Elephant Trunk (Hybrid)
points: Combines open arch surgery and distal stented endograft
Single-stage definitive repair for complex arch disease
Direct visual distal landing avoids vessel rupture

right.title: Conventional Elephant Trunk
points: Leaves non-stented soft Dacron sleeve in descending aorta
Mandates a second surgical or endovascular procedure
Risk of interval aortic rupture while awaiting stage 2

steps.say: Continuous intraoperative neuromonitoring is mandatory during arch reconstruction. Near-infrared spectroscopy measures real-time cerebral tissue oxygen saturation non-invasively. A drop greater than 20 percent from baseline triggers immediate hemodynamic evaluation, catheter repositioning, or increase in pump flow.
steps.tx: Intraoperative **near-infrared spectroscopy** provides continuous non-invasive **cerebral oximetry** across frontal cerebral cortices during circulatory arrest. A bilateral or unilateral **saturation drop threshold** exceeding 20 percent from baseline indicates inadequate perfusion, prompting immediate verification of cannula position, perfusion pressure, and pump flow rates.
